name: PT Trimegah Bangun Persada Tbk

frontmatter.title: Harita Nickel: costs reset, the multiple carries the call
frontmatter.summary: The nine months to September reset the cost base and the target follows it. The September benchmark revision is a cost cut, not a price cut, and the July dividend is no longer deducted twice. At the price the market implies nickel above our marker, so the DCF alone is below the last price and the EV/EBITDA leg carries the ADD: target Rp859.
thesis: The ore body is real and finite: five years of proven and probable reserve, valued with no terminal value and no credit for resources above the reserve.
The nine-month print carries a royalty and mining cost the FY2025 accounts did not, and the model now reproduces the actual margin rather than the prior year's.
The associates hold more value than the operations do, and their cash dividends are the only channel by which that value reaches shareholders.
Kepmen 363 cut the royalty base on the grade Harita sells, because ore is sold at the market price and taxed on the benchmark; the base carries the relief, the bear its reversal.
The rating is not a nickel call: the DCF alone sits below the price, and the multiple leg is what turns it into a return.
The risks that keep a discount in place are the ore quota, a free float below the new minimum and a controlling shareholder who owns most of the register.

catalysts.event: Government decision on the nickel ore quota for the coming year
FY2026 results and the dividend declaration, the first full-year print at the new cost base
First compliance deadline for the fifteen per cent minimum public float
First full year priced under the September corrective-factor schedule

blocks.text: This is an update: the target is **Rp859** against a last price of Rp750, an expected return of 18.8% of which Rp32 is dividend, and the rating is **ADD** [S0][S2].

Three things moved, all corrections of our own arithmetic. First, the cost base: the previous version rolled the nine-month revenue into FY2026E but left the FY2025 unit cost, producing a margin the actual print does not support, and the model now reproduces the actual — EBITDA margin of 27.1% against 34.7% in FY2025 [S0][S2]. Second, the September decree: we read it as close to neutral, and the source says the opposite — "penambang menjual bijih pada harga pasar tetapi membayar pajak berdasarkan HPM", miners sell at the market price and pay the tax on the benchmark — so it cuts the fiscal burden without touching what the ore fetches [S17]. Third, the bridge: the July dividend sits in the third-quarter cash flow and was already out of the September cash, so charging it again deducted money the company no longer had [S0].

The variant view is now a price, and we had it backwards in the last version. At the last price the reverse DCF implies nickel at US$18,451/t in FY2027E, 1.05 times the reviewed marker of US$17,500/t and well above the November spot of US$16,375/t [S0][S3]. The market is not capitalising a trough; it is paying slightly more for nickel than we assume. The consequence is plain: the primary DCF gives Rp661, below the Rp750 price, so the whole of the return rests on the EV/EBITDA leg at Rp1,133 and the small yield leg at Rp585 [S0]. We are not hiding that. On a life-of-asset DCF we would not own this at the price; on the level the operations trade at against peers we would, and the weighted target says the balance favours owning it.

PT Trimegah Bangun Persada is an Indonesian nickel producer controlled by PT Harita Jayaraya, which held 81.3% at the last year-end; the free float is 12.9% and the group employed 7,582 people [S2][S0]. Its business is an integrated complex on Obi Island: open-pit mines feed smelters and refineries inside one industrial estate, which the annual report presents as the core of the model because it removes the logistics and feedstock risk standalone smelters carry [S2].

The ore body has two layers feeding two routes. Limonite, at about 1.1 per cent nickel, goes to high-pressure acid leach plants producing mixed hydroxide precipitate, refined into nickel sulphate and cobalt sulphate for cathodes. Saprolite, the higher-grade ore, goes to rotary kiln electric furnaces for ferronickel [S2]. The AR publishes no saprolite assay, so the grade is derived from output: 188.6 kt of contained nickel in ferronickel over 12.1 million wet tonnes sold places it in the 1.5 to 1.7 per cent band of the benchmark ladder, and is a floor because recovery is below one [S2][S11][S13]. The split matters for valuation: the ferronickel route is consolidated, while the leach plants are associates, so most battery-chain exposure sits below the revenue line [S2].

The group sold 12.1 million wet tonnes of saprolite and 18.5 million of limonite in FY2025, with ferronickel sales of 188.6 kt of contained nickel against 130.6 kt of precipitate and sulphate from the associates [S2][F11][F12]. The reserve statement constrains the model: the MROR covers 3,859 of contained nickel in reserves and resources, but the audited tables give 84.2 million wet tonnes at Kawasi, 39.1 at GPS, 30.3 at GTS and 12.2 at JMP [S2][F23][F24][F25][F26]. That is 2,059 of contained nickel on our grade assumptions — five years of feed — and the resources above it are valued in no scenario, which is upside against the rating, not for it [S2].

Nickel is the pricing variable and the reviewed deck is the anchor. The house metals series carries nickel at US$15,162/t for FY2025A, US$17,089/t for FY2026E and a through-cycle marker of US$17,500/t from FY2027E, against a spot of US$16,375/t on 5 November [S0][S3]; the marker sits above spot because the deck assumes Indonesian supply discipline bites [S0][S6].

Policy is the dominant driver. The ministry settled this year's national ore quota at 290 million tonnes, above its early-year plan, said no additions would be granted, and for next year says only that it is watching exchange stocks [S6]. That quota, not the LME price, determines how much ore smelters can buy; early-November enforcement of ore-trading rules pushed the three-month price to a five-week high, showing how much of the price is policy [S3].

The size of that cut is in the September analysis we have now archived. Low-grade ore went from US$46.06 a wet tonne under the April formula to US$24.89, below the US$27.00 spot pays for the same grade, so the benchmark has moved from a ceiling above the market to a floor under it [S17]. That is a fiscal change: ore is sold at the market price and the royalty is computed on the benchmark, so at the 14 per cent rate the charge on that grade falls by about US$2.90 a wet tonne, leaving a residual thirty cents above the transaction-price basis [S17]. A lower benchmark does not lower the price Harita receives; it lowers what Harita pays, which is why the base carries the relief [S17]. The authors call it a partial reversal: the corrective factor remains above its pre-April level [S17].

The history is volume-led growth against a price headwind. Revenue rose 9.9% to IDR 29,633bn in FY2025, with EBITDA of IDR 10,272bn on our restated depreciation, net profit of IDR 10,970bn of which IDR 8,952bn accrued to shareholders, and return on equity of 25.9% [S2].

**The new period against our forecast.** The nine months to 30 September are actual. Revenue sits inside our FY2026E line of IDR 36,391bn, and we cut FY2026E volume to 400 kt against the 412 kt reserve-backed plan [S0]. The third quarter produced the strongest operating cash flow of the year after a first half close to nil, taking net debt off its June peak and lifting the associate book, and that is the balance sheet the valuation starts from [S0]. We do not read the quarter as a clean test of the benchmark revision, since it covered two weeks of September, and neither does the model [S17].

**Depreciation is the first thing to get right.** The pack's depreciation is only the charge booked to operating expenses; the LK's fixed-asset note reports the full allocation to cost of goods sold and opex, IDR 1,867bn for FY2025 against IDR 1,735bn for FY2024 [S2][F4][F5]. We use the LK figure, which lifts EBITDA and lowers EBIT while leaving reported net profit unchanged, because depreciation is a reclassification inside the same accounts; the segment note shows a slightly larger total again at IDR 1,892bn once right-of-use and mining-property amortisation are included, so our figure sits at the conservative end [S2]. Finance costs also need correcting: the LK shows finance costs of IDR 581bn and finance income of IDR 260bn, against a higher pack figure [S2][F6][F8].

**The associates, and a basis break we must disclose.** Their share of profit was IDR 4,091bn in FY2025, roughly a third of net profit, against a carrying value of IDR 23,679bn [S2][F15][F16]. The cash side is IDR 1,980bn of dividends received, which is what the forecast carries as non-operating income [S2][F17]. Booking the equity-accounted profit as cash would manufacture cash the group never receives, so the forecast is on a cash basis while the FY2025 reported EPS of Rp142 is on the equity-method basis. The apparent fall to Rp106 in FY2026E is therefore largely that basis change and not an earnings collapse: the equity income in the FY2025 figure is IDR 4,091bn of non-cash profit, the nine-month attributable print is struck on the same equity-included basis, and on cash earnings the forecast year is close to the prior one. The dividend comparison inherits the same break: the FY2025 DPS of Rp43 was struck on reported earnings, while the FY2026E DPS of Rp32 is the model's payout on cash EPS, so the 4.2% yield understates the dividend capacity the associates fund [S2][S0]. We chose the cash basis because it is the only one the DCF can use, and we flag rather than smooth it.

**The cost build, rebuilt on the nine-month print.** FY2025 cost of goods sold of IDR 19,941bn contained royalty of IDR 1,446bn and restated depreciation; stripping both gave the cash cost per contained tonne the previous version held flat for five years [S2][F13]. The nine months say it is stale: revenue per contained tonne ROSE against FY2025, so the whole margin compression is cost, and the model now carries US$3,570 a tonne including royalty [S0]. FY2026E EBITDA falls to IDR 9,869bn and the DCF follows it. Two forward changes are sourced. The September decree is worth about US$2.90 a wet tonne on the limonite grade; on the limonite tonnage the source describes that aggregate is what we benchmark against, but the model carries the relief from FY2027E at its per-tonne rate rather than in full, in the mining cost line rather than in the royalty rate, so that EBITDA and cash flow are identical whichever line carries it [S17][F57]. And from FY2028E the unit cost is escalated with the house rupiah inflation assumption of 3.3%, which is what holding cost flat in real terms means; the previous version's flat nominal dollar line was an unsourced real-terms cut [S0].

**Working capital.** Net working capital was IDR 3,353bn at the year-end on revenue of IDR 29,633bn, and at 30 September it is 18.3% of trailing revenue, which is the ratio the model holds [S0]. The build is inventory: it rose by about three quarters in nine months while nine-month cost of goods sold already exceeded all of FY2025, so this is not a slower-selling pile, and the two readings are ore held for a higher fourth-quarter sales rate and lower-grade material awaiting a buyer, neither disclosed [S0]. Holding the September ratio defers cash the previous version released, and that charge is right: we can see the inventory and not the buyer. The balance sheet is comfortable — net debt of IDR 3,364bn at the year-end, total equity of IDR 46,756bn including minorities, and cash rebuilt at September [S2][S0].

Our forecast is deliberately dull: 400 kt of contained nickel rolled to the nine-month print, 412 kt held to FY2030E because that is what the reserve supports, revenue of IDR 36,391bn and IDR 40,088bn, EBITDA of IDR 12,245bn, and EPS of Rp106 and Rp132 [S2][S0]. The FY2025 volume of 392 kt is the company's own 12.1 million wet tonnes of saprolite and 18.5 million of limonite at a derived saprolite grade and the disclosed limonite floor of 1.1 per cent [S2]. The step over FY2025 is sourced to GTS, a new mine that began operating in the third quarter of 2025, and to the RKEF associate KPS running its eight lines at capacity, which reaches us as saprolite sold rather than consolidated ferronickel [S2][S14].

The calibration gate prices FY2026E at the FY2025A benchmark and volume and compares it with FY2025A EBITDA; it reproduces well under two thirds of that figure and the gap is cost, not arithmetic [S2]. The FY2025 EBITDA of IDR 10,272bn is the engine's restated EBIT plus LK depreciation, and its EBIT sits a fraction of a per cent above the LK operating profit of IDR 8,385bn because the model nets other operating items inside costs, so the baseline is right [S2][F45]. Volume is not the driver: the FY2026E step is a couple of per cent. A reader who wants the prior year's EBITDA back should want the prior year's royalty schedule with it, and that is not the world the nine-month print describes [S0][S17].

**Earnings-quality flags.** Equity-accounted income is a third of profit and not cash, which is why we model the dividends [S2][F15][F17]. Operating cash flow was below net profit in FY2025, a working-capital and non-cash-income effect rather than an accrual problem, but a reminder that reported profit overstates distributable cash [S0][S2]. Minorities took IDR 2,019bn, so the parent's share is materially below the group's [S2]. And related-party trade receivables are a large share of total receivables, a flow to monitor [S2].

We value NCKL on a life-of-asset discounted cash flow at through-cycle nickel, the house method for commodity producers: the reserve is finite, price dominates, and a current-year multiple would capitalise wherever the cycle sits [S2]. The DCF discounts explicit annual free cash flow over the proven and probable reserve only — 2,059 of contained nickel, five years at plan volume, ending FY2030E — with no terminal value, so the value is what the company can actually mine [S2][F28].

The cost of capital comes from the house parameters: a cost of equity of 14.4% on a levered beta of 1.27 and a country risk premium of 2.5%, and a pre-tax cost of debt of 9.4% against the 6.2% the accounts imply, which is conservative; with equity at 83% of the mix the WACC is 13.2% [S0][S2].

The primary DCF gives Rp661 per share on enterprise value of IDR 28,454bn [S0]. We add the associate stake at its 30 September carrying value less an expected mark-down, and deduct net debt and the minority interest. NOT the dividend: the FY2025 dividend went ex in July and the payment sits in the third-quarter cash flow, so it is already out of the September cash the bridge starts from; the previous version deducted it twice [S0]. There is no terminal value and no value for ore beyond the reserve, so the bull is a better price or better volume, not a longer life [S2].

**The associates.** The FY2025 equity income of IDR 4,091bn capitalised at our 14.4% cost of equity reproduces the carrying value used in the bridge and sits above the audited year-end book of IDR 23,679bn [S2][F15][F16]; on the September balance the two agree, so there is no mark-up to argue about. What book does not capture is a write-down, carried as an EXPECTED value: in the bear their earnings and dividends halve, so half the carrying value is unsupported, and that half weighted at the bear's probability is the mark-down line [S2][F16].

**Cross-checks.** The EV/EBITDA method gives Rp1,133, 71.3% above the DCF, at a peer median of 7.5 times [S0]. The gap is the life, not the level: a multiple capitalises earnings in perpetuity, while the DCF gives five years of reserve and no terminal value at a WACC over thirteen per cent. Both legs share one bridge, so the operations and the stake are counted once [S0]. A caveat: the metric is the pack's last-twelve-month EBITDA, struck on the understated depreciation we restate elsewhere, which biases this value down and is why the weight stays at the house level [S0][S2]. The dividend-capacity cross-check gives Rp585, -11.5% against the DCF, because the peer yield is applied to a payout on cash-basis EPS that the associates fund but the model does not gross up; it is the trough-dividend reading of the same asset and we weight it at a monitoring level rather than as a valuation leg [S0][S2]. Price-to-book is dropped: most of the book it would mark is the associate investment the DCF already carries at book, so the leg re-marks one asset twice, and the engine cannot mark book ex-associates [S0][S2].

The bridge is explicit: operations at IDR 28,454bn, plus the associate stake at the 30 September balance, less the expected mark-down, less net debt and the non-controlling interest at the same date [S0][S2]. Nothing else is charged; a special dividend, disposal or rights issue since the balance-sheet date would be a bridge line and we searched for none [S0]. The minority is handled once, because the P&L already charges the minorities' share of profit. One disclosure: the September investments balance is above the audited year-end book of IDR 23,679bn by roughly a quarter, which three quarters of equity-accounted profit explains in part; a capital contribution would explain the rest, no disclosure states one, and the direction of the error is down [S0][S2][F16].

**What the price implies.** The reverse DCF says the shares discount nickel at US$18,451/t in FY2027E, 1.05 times the reviewed marker of US$17,500/t and about a tenth above the 5 November spot of US$16,375/t [S0][S3]. That is not a trough: on our nickel path the primary DCF of Rp661 is below the Rp750 price, so the shares are expensive on reserve value and cheap on the level the operations trade at — 5.8x times our FY2026E EBITDA and 1.1x times book, with a dividend yield of 4.2% [S0]. Our ADD is therefore a statement about the multiple, not about nickel: we are not forecasting a re-rating from a trough, we are saying the reserve is worth less than the price while the operating level is worth more, and the EV/EBITDA leg is what carries the target [S0].

items: **Nickel price (high likelihood, high impact).** The market is in surplus and Indonesian capacity keeps growing; a price stuck at the November level or below cuts revenue directly and is the bear's first shock [S2][S3].

**Ore quota (medium likelihood, high impact).** The ministry fixed this year's national quota above its early plan and barred additions, and is watching exchange stocks before next year's; a lower quota or a cut to NCKL's own permits cuts volume rather than price [S6][F20].

**Associate dependence (medium likelihood, high impact).** A third of profit and more than half the market capitalisation rest on equity-accounted companies whose carrying value a precipitate margin collapse would test [S2][F15][F16]. The bear halves their dividends — the cash channel the DCF carries — and the capital channel is the expected mark-down in the bridge, sized from the same event without stacking [S2].

**Governance and float (medium likelihood, high impact).** The controlling shareholder holds the great majority of the register and the free float of 12.9% is below the fifteen per cent the regulator requires, with first compliance in March 2027; a placement would dilute, a sell-down would change the register [S15][S16][S2].
**Operational (low likelihood, medium impact).** Captive coal power, an industrial port and acid leach plants mean an outage, residue incident or weather event would hit volume [S2].

**Currency (low likelihood, low impact).** Revenue and cash cost are both dollar-denominated, so the rupiah mainly translates the dividend and reported earnings rather than changing the economics [S0][S2].

**Regulatory cost (medium likelihood, high impact).** Royalty and tax regimes have been revised repeatedly; the royalty line is the LK's effective rate on revenue, the September relief is in the cost base, and a return to the April schedule is the bear's shock [S2][F13][S17].

**Benchmark formula and grade (in force, medium impact).** The September decree pulled the low-grade quote to US$24.89 against a spot market of US$27.00; a further revision reaching the 1.3 per cent bracket, or a grade slip putting more tonnage under the threshold, would reach revenue where this one only reached cost [S17][S13].

blocks.text: The bear cuts nickel a fifth, volume a tenth and the associate dividend by half, and adds the one shock the bull cannot mirror: a return to the April royalty schedule, which existed until September, worth about a trillion rupiah on the limonite tonnage [S17][F54][F57]. There is no announced schedule below the September one, so a mirrored royalty cut in the bull would be invented, and we keep the asymmetry and say so [S17]. The bull lifts nickel a fifth, volume a tenth and the associate dividend to double, and values the shares at Rp1,149; the base is Rp859 and the bear Rp571 [S0][S6]. Realisation is a fixed ratio of the benchmark, so a fifth on the benchmark is a fifth on revenue in both directions, and the old separate realisation shock was dropped because the September analysis shows the ladder is not the price the ore transacts on [S17].

Ownership is concentrated: PT Harita Jayaraya held 81.3% at the last year-end, insiders hold 86.9% on the pack's classification, and the free float is 12.9% [S2][S0]. The regulator has raised the minimum public float to fifteen per cent in stages, with first compliance in March 2027 [S15][S16]; the float falls short, and closing the gap means a dilutive placement or a controlling-holder sell-down. We hold no dated index announcement and price neither [S0]. The FY2025 accounts were audited with an unqualified opinion by a member firm of a global network, and related-party transactions are disclosed; the largest flow is the related-party trade receivable, which we monitor because related-party sales can flatter revenue and receivables alike [S2]. The dividend record is short but rising — IDR 1,914bn paid in FY2025 — and the company retired 110.7 million shares into treasury, which reduces the count without changing control [S2][S4][F18]. On a cash basis the FY2025 distribution was struck on earnings that included unrealised associate income, which is the one governance-adjacent flag we carry on the payout [S2][F15].

The calendar above is the model's test schedule, one line per defect the base case could suffer. The quota decision expected in the fourth quarter of 2026 is the volume test: a national quota below this year's reaches NCKL through its own permit and through the RKEF associates, and the ministry's monthly benchmark releases show the grade bands Harita sells into [S6][S17]. The February FY2026 print is the cost test, the first full year struck at the nine-month cost base, and the dividend declaration travels with it, where the payout on cash earnings against the reported equity-included EPS is the number that matters [S4][S2]. The March 2027 deadline is the register test, and a placement and a controlling-holder sell-down are not the same event for the share count [S16]. In the first half of 2027 the September corrective-factor schedule gets its first full year, and the April schedule it replaced is exactly what the bear's royalty shock restores [S17].

What we watch between dates: contained-nickel volume against the 412 kt plan; cash cost per contained tonne against the 3,570 the model now carries; associate dividends received, the DCF's only cash channel; inventory, which is where the September cash went; and the free float at 12.9% against the regulator's minimum [S0][S2][S15]. The 5.8x times multiple carries the ADD and the Rp859 target, so an EBITDA miss narrows the leg the DCF is not holding up [S0]. A reversal of the September relief would show in the benchmark release before it showed in the price, and it would move value against us [S17].

valuation.label: DCF to end of life (no terminal value)

bear.narrative: Three things go wrong together. The 2027 RKAB review turns into a cut to NCKL's own ore quota and the persistent global surplus the company describes in its own annual review keeps LME nickel near the 2024-2025 trough, so the ore and ferronickel prices fall with it. The fiscal reversal lands on top: the September corrective-factor cut is undone, the royalty base returns to the April HPM and the group pays about IDR 0.85trn more on the same tonnage (S17). The associates earn less - their HPAL margin is the most price-sensitive part of the chain (S12) - so their dividends to the group halve, which is the cash channel the model carries; the capital channel is carried in the bridge as an expected mark-down of the stake, sized at half its carrying value under this case and weighted by this case's probability, not stacked on the dividend cut. Volume a tenth below base and a nickel price a fifth below the deck.

bull.narrative: Indonesia enforces the 2027 quota cut and the ore-trade crackdown that lifted the LME price in early November, tightening global supply into a stainless and battery demand recovery; NCKL's low-cost Obi ore and its 240kt RKEF / 120kt HPAL base run at capacity, the associates' MHP margins recover and pay double the dividends, and the through-cycle nickel marker holds above US$17,500/t. THE PRICE LEG IS THE MIRROR OF THE BEAR, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OF IT (corrected 2026-11-12, answering C6). The old x1.07 realisation shock was sourced from a full move of the ore leg to the published HPM ladder, and S17 establishes that the ladder is not the transaction price - miners sell at the market price and the benchmark sat USD 17-18/wmt ABOVE it under the April formula and USD 2.11 above it now ([S17], USD 24.89 against USD 27.00). A price ladder the company does not transact on is not a bull case, so the ladder is not used and the realised ratio is not moved: the bull carries a 20% higher benchmark, mirrored by the bear's 20% lower one, and because realisation is a fixed ratio of the benchmark that is a full 20% on the revenue line. Volume a tenth above base is the GTS and KPS ramp, not resource conversion: the 144.95m wmt of resources above the proven and probable reserve (310.8m less 165.85m, S2 p.112) are valued in NO scenario, and the target says so - the 10% volume step is the last of the reserve life, not the first of the resources.

assumptions.label: Sales volume plan
assumptions.basis: FY2027E-FY2030E 412 kt contained Ni, held flat; FY2026E 400 kt, rolled to the nine-month actual. The plan is the volume the proven+probable reserve supports: 165.85m wmt remaining at 31 December 2025 (F23-F26) over five years is 33.2m wmt a year, 1.24% blended grade = 412 kt contained Ni. FY2025 actual was 392.1 kt (F1), so the plan is +5%, in line with first-half 2026 revenue of IDR 17.1trn being 21% above the IDR 14.1trn of first-half 2025 against a nickel price roughly 13% higher (S5); the drivers are GTS's first full year and the KPS phase 1-2 lines (S2 p.112). FY2026E is cut to 400 kt because the nine months to 30 September are now actual: IDR 26,868bn of revenue, IDR 9,771bn of it in the third quarter, so the fourth quarter at the third-quarter run-rate gives IDR 36,639bn for the year against the IDR 37,483bn the 412 kt path implies, and 400 kt reproduces the actual-led year to within 0.5% (S0). That is a roll to the print, not a downgrade of the plan: the reserve-backed 412 kt still governs FY2027E onward. No growth beyond the reserve is assumed: the 144.95m wmt of resources above reserves (310.8m less the 165.85m of proven and probable, S2 p.112) is valued in no scenario, base or bull, and the 2027 national quota review is a risk rather than a sourced cut to NCKL's own RKAB (F20; S6). No volume decline is assumed.

assumptions.label: Realised price / benchmark
assumptions.basis: Calibrated on the last actual: FY2025 revenue of IDR 29,632.8bn (S2 p.284) over 392.1 kt of contained nickel sold at the deck's FY2025A nickel average of US$15,162/t and USD/IDR 16,448 gives US$4,595 of revenue per contained nickel tonne, a realisation of 0.3030. The ratio is held flat across the forecast, not fitted to the FY2026E deck level: it is a structural blend of ore sold at HPM-linked prices (a fraction of metal value) and ferronickel sold at a discount to LME (segment split S2 note 37: processing IDR 22,454.7bn external, mining IDR 7,178.1bn external and IDR 2,932.5bn inter-segment, F38-F40). WHY THE REFORM IS NOT ADDED ON TOP (update 2026-11-09). The ore leg is priced off the HPM ladder; at the second half of October the ladder gives US$54.48-59.12 a wet tonne for saprolite and US$22.76-25.33 for limonite (F30/F31/F42/F43, S13), against an average realised ore price of US$20.10 a wet tonne across all 30.59m wmt in FY2025 (F38-F40 over F1, at the FY2025 rate) - so the published schedule is well above what the accounts realised, which is what the 100-140% reform claim refers to. The model does not gross that up because the reported first half, priced under the April formula, booked IDR 17.1trn of revenue (F29, S5/S14): doubled, that is below the revenue this realisation produces for FY2026E, so the actuals do not show an incremental reform lift on top of volume, price and FX. Trade press also records smelters buying below the benchmark (S13). The upside that would follow a full pass- through of the saprolite leg to the top of the ladder is carried in the bull case as a realisation shock, and the downside of a grade slip under the low-grade threshold in the bear, so the reform is in the valuation in both directions rather than absent from it. Any mix shift is disclosed in section 4; we do not add a haircut on top of the observed blend.

assumptions.label: Strip ratio (bcm per tonne) or cost-intensity factor
assumptions.basis: Set to 1.0: this is an ore-to-nickel-unit model, not a coal-style bcm stripping model, so cost_per_bcm carries the mining cash cost per contained nickel tonne directly. The AR describes open-cast mining on Obi but does not publish a strip ratio (S2 p.112), so no unsourced intensity drift is modelled.

assumptions.label: Mining cost per bcm (or per unit when intensity is 1)
assumptions.basis: REBUILT ON THE NINE-MONTH PRINT (2026-11-12, answering C1). The cost base is no longer the FY2025 unit cost: the nine months to 30 September 2026 are actual and they carry a different cost structure. Revenue IDR 26,868.3bn, cost of goods sold IDR 20,125.0bn and opex IDR 1,059.4bn on the data pack (S0, 2026Q1+Q2+Q3), with the LK D&A basis of IDR 4,761m per kt (da_unit, below) giving D&A of IDR 1,428.5bn for the nine months, leave EBITDA of IDR 7,112bn - a 26.47% EBITDA margin and a 25.1% gross margin (COGS over revenue 74.9%), against the 32.7% gross and 34.7% EBITDA margin of FY2025. The model now reproduces that margin: total cash cost excluding royalty and D&A is US$3,351/t of contained nickel, which is 26.47% of the modelled US$5,178/t revenue per contained tonne after the flat royalty (4.88%) and opex (3.94%) lines. The FY2025 comparison (US$2,578/t, IDR 16,628.7bn of COGS less royalty IDR 1,445.7bn less D&A IDR 1,867.0bn over 392.1 kt, F13/F4/F1) is therefore superseded by the actual: unit cost in dollars rose, and the nine months show it. Mining is 25% of the total and processing 75%, the segment split of the FY2025 cost base (mining COGS IDR 5,532.5bn of IDR 19,941.4bn consolidated, S2 p.396), so US$838/t mining and US$2,513/t processing. FY2026E carries the nine-month level; FY2027E-FY2030E carry it less the royalty delta below (US$3,295/t), flat in nominal dollars - a real-terms decline, and the neutral choice for a miner with no dollar cost index in the house decks (macro carries usd_idr, dxy, bi_rate, cpi_id; none is a dollar mining cost series). The one sourced forward change sits in the total: Kepmen 363 cut the limonite royalty base from the April HPM to the revised one, worth about US$2.8-2.9/wmt (US$53m a year on the sourced tonnage, [S17][F57]). The model carries US$75/t of contained nickel, about US$31m a year on 412 kt: a partial carry of that aggregate, stated as such - carried here rather than in royalty_rate, which stays at the LK's effective rate, so that EBITDA and cash flow are identical either way and the split is a disclosure choice.

assumptions.label: Other cash cost per unit (haul, barge, process)
assumptions.basis: Processing share of the same rebuilt cash cost: US$2,513/t of contained nickel in FY2026E and US$2,445-2,459/t in FY2027E-FY2030E, from the same nine-month reconciliation as the mining line (COGS IDR 20,125.0bn less LK D&A of IDR 1,428.5bn and less the flat 4.88% royalty, over the nine-month contained-nickel tonnage that the IDR 26,868.3bn of revenue implies at the modelled US$5,178/t). It covers smelting, power, hauling and barging for the ore the group processes itself. Held flat in nominal dollars: no dollar cost index exists in the house decks, the LK has not published a unit cost, and escalating it would be an unsourced drift on top of a base that already carries the actual step-up. Fuel sensitivity enters through fuel_share on the mining line and through the rupiah. The modelled margin widening from FY2028E to FY2030E comes from the reviewed nickel deck's own drift (US$17,500 to US$17,850 in FY2030E) and the FX path, not from a cost assumption. Where the royalty sits: the flat 4.88% line is the LK's own effective rate, so the residual royalty burden the nine-month print carries (the April HPM formula, 41% above the ad-valorem rate on limonite, [S17]) is inside these two cost lines; the assembly is a decomposition of one total, and only the total is calibrated.

assumptions.label: Fuel share of mining cost
assumptions.basis: Coal-fired captive power and diesel haulage are a minority of the mining line; 0.15 keeps the ici4 link alive without letting the coal deck drive a nickel miner's cost base. Non-key knob.

assumptions.label: Royalty rate (flat regimes)
assumptions.basis: Flat 4.88% of revenue, the effective rate the FY2025 cash-flow statement shows: royalty paid IDR 1,445.7bn against revenue IDR 29,632.8bn (F13, S2 p.287/p.284). It is the LK's own effective rate, not a statutory assumption, and it is flat because the model prices a blended ore-plus-product revenue line rather than a single mineral benchmark band. The post-revision royalty change is not double counted here: the 14% rate on the HPM is paid on the benchmark, not on the modelled revenue, and after Kepmen 363 that benchmark sits USD 0.30/wmt above the ad-valorem basis (S17/F57), so the residual is inside the cost lines - see cost_per_bcm, where the US$2.8-2.9/wmt relief is carried. What the rate does NOT capture is a reversion to the April formula, which would add about IDR 0.85trn of royalty on the same tonnage [S17]; that is a bear shock, so the base is not asked to carry a risk the fiscal calendar has already removed.

assumptions.label: Other revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default constant; the model's revenue is the full consolidated line

assumptions.label: Gross margin on other revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default constant

assumptions.label: D&A per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 depreciation and amortisation of IDR 1,866,965m (IDR 1,780,167m in cost of goods sold, IDR 86,356m in SG&A and IDR 442m mining properties, F4) over 392.1 kt contained nickel = IDR 4,761m per kt. Held flat in nominal rupiah: the asset base is mature (fixed assets IDR 22,549.0bn) and the group capitalises new smelter capacity inside its associates, not in the consolidated entity.

assumptions.label: Sustaining capex per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 capex of IDR 939.4bn (fixed-asset additions IDR 577.7bn plus payables paid IDR 331.3bn, exploration and evaluation IDR 19.1bn and mining properties IDR 11.3bn, S2 p.287) over 392.1 kt = IDR 2,396m per kt. FY2024 was IDR 1,305bn, so the level is maintenance spend on an installed base, not a project cycle; held flat. Project capex sits inside the associates (HPL, ONC, KPS) and is therefore not charged to the consolidated DCF.

assumptions.label: Other capex (expansion projects)
assumptions.basis: engine default constant; no consolidated expansion project is announced

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Rolled to the September actual (2026-11-12, answering C9): net working capital of IDR 6,239.9bn at 30 September 2026 over LTM revenue of IDR 34,098.5bn = 18.30% (S0), against IDR 3,352.9bn at 31 December 2025 (11.31% of FY2025 revenue - the ratio this line used to carry). The build is real and is carried, not assumed away: inventory went from IDR 5,875.8bn to IDR 10,304.7bn (+75%) in the nine months while receivables rose from IDR 1,937.9bn to IDR 2,647.8bn and payables from IDR 1,808.4bn to IDR 2,925.2bn (S0). Nine-month COGS of IDR 20,125.0bn already exceeds the whole of FY2025 (IDR 19,941.4bn), so the stock is not simply a slower-selling pile; the two readings are ore held for a higher third-quarter sales run-rate and lower-grade material awaiting a buyer, and neither is disclosed. Holding 18.3% makes the base release no working capital it cannot see: the step from 11.3% to 18.3% charges IDR 2.5trn of cash to FY2026E. The sensitivity is in section 3.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: FY2025 income tax of IDR 1,184.6bn over pre-tax profit from operations of IDR 8,084.6bn (EBIT IDR 8,405.1bn less net finance cost IDR 320.4bn, S2 p.284) = 14.7%; 15% is used, the rate the audited accounts show, not the 22% statutory rate. The low cash rate reflects the associate income that is taxed at source and the mining tax allowances.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 finance costs IDR 580.7bn (F6) over FY2024 closing debt IDR 9,380.5bn = 6.2%; held at 6.2%. Gross debt was IDR 8,915.8bn at 30 June 2026 against cash of IDR 4,885.7bn (S0), i.e. NET DEBT of IDR 4,030.0bn, not a net cash position; the rate is on gross debt either way.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: FY2025 finance income IDR 260.2bn (F8) over FY2024 closing cash IDR 6,486.4bn = 4.0%; held at 4.0%.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Debt is flat to falling: gross debt IDR 9,380.5bn at FY2025 and IDR 8,915.8bn at 30 June 2026 (S0), with operating cash flow of IDR 8,601bn covering capex and the dividend. No new facility is announced, so net borrowing is zero.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Cash dividends received from associates, IDR 1,980.2bn in FY2025 (F17, S2 p.287), held flat. The equity-method share of associate profit (IDR 4,090.7bn, F15) is deliberately NOT carried in the cash flow: it is unrealised and the associate stakes are valued separately at their carrying value through the investments line in section 4, so including it would double-count and would manufacture cash the group never receives.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: FY2025 non-controlling interests of IDR 2,018.8bn over net profit of IDR 10,970.3bn = 18.4% (S2 p.285); held at 18.4%.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: FY2025 DPS of Rp42.64 over EPS of Rp142.02 is 30% (S0; S2 p.285), the third consecutive year of a rising dividend (Rp22.19, Rp26.72, Rp30.36). That FY2025 distribution, IDR 2.7trn in total, was paid in July 2026 (S4). Held at 30%; the payout is covered by cash flow without new debt.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Zero. The 2025 buyback retired 110.7m shares into treasury (0.18% of the 62.99bn outstanding, F18, S2 p.17); we do not extrapolate a buyback that has no announced programme.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: The primary method is a life-of-asset DCF with no terminal value, so this parameter is inert; it is set at the house rupiah long-run rate for completeness (macro deck).

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Rolled to the nine-month actual (2026-11-12): SG&A and other operating expenses of IDR 1,059.4bn on revenue of IDR 26,868.3bn (S0, 2026Q1+Q2+Q3) = 3.94%, against 4.41% for FY2025 (IDR 1,306.8bn on IDR 29,632.8bn, S2 p.284). The latest actual is the anchor; the ratio is lower because revenue grew faster than overhead, which is what a fixed cost base does at higher volumes.

challenges.challenge: The update rolls in Q3 revenue and volume but not Q3 costs. FY2026E EBITDA of IDR 14,533bn assumes COGS of IDR 22,161bn (39.1% gross margin); the 9M2026 actual is revenue IDR 26,868bn, COGS IDR 20,125bn (25.1% gross margin), opex IDR 1,059bn and, on the LK D&A basis, EBITDA of about IDR 7.1trn. Annualised at Q3 that is about IDR 9.7trn, so the model year is ~50% higher and Q4 would need ~IDR 7.4trn against the Q3 IDR 2.6trn. The FY2027E-FY2030E years inherit the same FY2025 unit cost of USD 2,578/t while S17 cites rising mining costs.
challenges.answer: Cost base rebuilt on the 9M print: cash cost US$3,351/t (US$3,317 FY2026E, US$3,295 forward), EBITDA margin 26.5% and gross 25.1% reproduced; FY2026E EBITDA 14,533 to 9,868; calibration gap now stated as -39%.

challenges.challenge: The load-bearing judgement of the update - that realisation is deliberately unchanged because a lower benchmark reduces what the mining segment receives on the same tonnes - is the opposite of what S17 says. S17 states that miners sell ore at market prices and pay royalty on the HPM ("penambang menjual bijih pada harga pasar tetapi membayar pajak berdasarkan HPM"), quotes the actual limonite price at USD 27.00 against the new HPM of USD 24.89, and quantifies the practical effect as a USD 2.8-2.9/wmt cut in the royalty and tax burden. The base therefore omits a sourced cost saving while asserting a revenue effect the source denies.
challenges.answer: S17 quoted verbatim: miners sell ore at the market price and pay royalty on the HPM. Realisation not re-based; the US$2.8-2.9/wmt relief is carried as a US$55/t cost cut from FY2027E and its reversal is the bear royalty shock.

challenges.challenge: The FY2025 dividend is deducted twice. Ex-date 9 July 2026, IDR 42.64/share, and the 2026Q3 dividends_paid line is IDR 2,687.6bn, so the payment is already out of the 30 September cash of IDR 6,128.2bn that gives the bridge net debt of IDR 3,466.0bn. The bridge then deducts IDR 2,700bn again at 1.0 probability, contradicting the statement that it had already left the company in July, before this balance sheet. The error understates equity value by Rp42.9/share, 4.2% of the target.
challenges.answer: Dividend bridge line deleted. The July payment is inside the 30 September cash through the Q3 dividends_paid line, so charging it again double counted Rp42.9 a share.

challenges.challenge: The associate mark-down is scenario-invariant. In the bear the associate earnings halve, so the full IDR 14,661bn is unsupported, but the bridge charges only the 25%-weighted IDR 3,665bn in every scenario. The bear value is therefore overstated by about Rp175/share (Rp672 against roughly Rp439 on its own logic), while the base and bull are penalised by a loss that belongs to the bear. Net, the probability-weighted target is overstated by about Rp30/share.
challenges.answer: The expected-value bridge is algebraically exact: the sum of p_s times (V_s less bridge) equals the bear-only charge, so the weighted target is unchanged. The per-scenario display bias is now disclosed.

challenges.challenge: The calibration reconciliation is arithmetically wrong. The report says that at the FY2025A volume the model own economics give IDR 10,272bn and that the gap the gate reports is the volume step; the engine prints ebitda_model 10,948.8 at volume 392.1 and gap_pct 6.59. The volume step is +2.0%, and the residual is the FY2026 rupiah translation (about 17,570 against 16,448).
challenges.answer: Calibration prose rewritten: the engine prints ebitda_model 6,223 at 392.1 kt against 10,272 actual, a -39.4% gap that is the cost reset from the 9M print, not the volume step.

challenges.challenge: The bull realisation shock of x1.07 is a third of a move the report itself sizes at +21% on the blended realisation (+89% on the ore leg to the published ladder). No source is given for taking a third. The bear, by contrast, takes the full low-grade benchmark cut (-7% on the blended realisation). The asymmetry is disclosed but not justified and caps the bull.
challenges.answer: Bull realisation shock removed. S17 shows the HPM ladder is a benchmark the ore does not transact on, so the price leg is the mirrored benchmark x1.2 and x0.8, not a third of the ladder.

challenges.challenge: The report calls the resources above the reserve the bull conversion path, but the bull adds only volume x1.10 for one year; 144.95m wmt (310.8m less the 165.85m of P+P, not the 131.9m stated) - 87% of the reserve tonnage - is valued nowhere. The associate stake is 62% of market cap and is not marked above book in the bull even when its HPAL margins recover.
challenges.answer: Resource tonnage corrected to 144.95m wmt (310.8 less 165.85) and the bull-conversion claim dropped: resources above the reserve are valued in no scenario, base or bull.

challenges.challenge: The scenarios have no fiscal shock. The base royalty is the FY2025 effective 4.88% of revenue (IDR 1,446bn); Kepmen 144 raised the limonite royalty burden by 41% (USD 2.61/wmt) before Kepmen 363 removed most of it, and S17 leaves a residual USD 0.30/wmt above the actual-price basis. A reversion to the April schedule would take roughly USD 2.6/wmt off 18.5m wmt, about IDR 850bn of EBITDA, and the bear does not test it.
challenges.answer: Bear gains a royalty shock of x1.43 on the royalty line, about IDR 0.85trn, being a return to the April Kepmen 144 schedule; the asymmetry against the bull is justified in qc.

challenges.challenge: Earnings quality is not screened on the balance sheet. Inventory rose from IDR 5,876bn to IDR 10,305bn (+75%) in the nine months while 9M COGS (IDR 20,125bn) already exceed the whole of FY2025 (IDR 19,941bn); NWC rose from IDR 3,353bn to IDR 6,240bn and is 18.3% of LTM revenue against the 11.3% the model holds. The base therefore assumes about IDR 1.6trn of working capital is released, and the inventory build is a divergence flag under the house screen.
challenges.answer: NWC rolled to the September actual at 18.30% of LTM revenue from 11.31%; the inventory build of about three quarters and its two readings are stated, cash conversion is a risk bullet.

challenges.challenge: The summary opens "We initiate coverage" in an update that four paragraphs later says the target is lower than the one published last week (v4, Rp1,067). The QC justification also says 3.3x FY2026E EV/EBITDA where the model prints 3.48x.
challenges.answer: Report opens as an update citing the prior version, and the 3.3x EV/EBITDA error is gone from the extreme_call justification, which now describes the rebuilt cost base.

challenges.challenge: F3 (3,859.02 kt Ni) and F28 (2,059.261 kt Ni) contain no such figures in the cited S2 text; they are derived from wet tonnes and a documented but assumed 1.2416% grade. The report presents 2,059 of contained nickel as coming from the audited IUP tables. 131.9m wmt of resources above reserves matches no figure in the source (310.8 - 165.85 = 144.95).
challenges.answer: Contained nickel is now labelled as derived at a stated grade from wet tonnes, and the resource figure is corrected to 144.95m wmt with the reserve table cited.

challenges.challenge: Section 7 'Catalysts and monitoring' is still a bare heading: fund record ends at the title, so the update would publish with an empty top-level section. QC round 2 (Q12) named this a sign-off blocker.
challenges.answer: Section 7 written: dated catalysts (Q4 quota decision, February FY2026 print and dividend, March 2027 float deadline, FY2027 first full year on the September schedule) plus the volume, cash-cost, associate-dividend, inventory and float monitors, all cited [S4][S6][S16][S17].

challenges.challenge: Section 3 still renders the cost escalator as 'the house rupiah inflation assumption of 328.0%': it interpolates deck.macro.cpi_id.FY2028E through the pct filter, while the model escalates unit cost 3.31% a year (mining 738.0 to 813.6, processing 2,444.6 to 2,694.7). As written the report states costs rise 328% a year on the line the whole update turns on.
challenges.answer: The deck CPI now renders through pctv, so the sentence reads 3.3% a year, matching the model's 3.31% unit-cost escalation; the pct filter had multiplied the already-percent deck value by 100 [S0].

challenges.challenge: The royalty relief is carried at three sizes and section 3 claims it is carried 'in full'. The model mining line falls US$75.1/t (813.1 to 738.0, about US$31m on 412 kt); the cost_per_bcm basis text states US$23m (US$55/t); F57/S17 give US$2.8-2.9/wmt on 18.5m wmt, about US$53m. The gap between model and F57 is about IDR 0.37trn of EBITDA and is unreconciled.
challenges.answer: One figure now stated: the model carries US$75/t of contained nickel, about US$31m on 412 kt, a partial carry of F57's US$2.8-2.9/wmt (about US$53m); both basis passages reconciled and section 3 no longer claims it is carried in full [S17][F57].

missing_bull_case.note: The bull carries only a third of the realisation pass-through the report itself quantifies (+7% against +21% blended, +89% on the ore leg) with no source for the haircut, and the resources above the reserve (144.95m wmt, not the 131.9m stated) are called the bull conversion path but add only volume x1.10 for one year. The associate stake, 62% of market cap, is not marked above book even in the bull whose narrative has HPAL margins recovering.

missing_bear_case.note: No fiscal leg: the base royalty is the FY2025 4.88% effective rate, the April Kepmen 144 raised the limonite burden 41% [S17] and the bear has no royalty or cost shock. The associate impairment is understated (see C4), and the 9M2026 working-capital build - inventory 5,876 to 10,305 (+75%) while COGS ran at a full-year rate, NWC/revenue 18.3% vs the 11.3% the model holds - is in neither the base nor the bear.

assumption_realism.note: The Q3 roll-in is revenue-only. FY2026E EBITDA of IDR 14,533bn implies a 39.1% gross margin against the 9M2026 actual of 25.1% (COGS IDR 20,125bn on revenue IDR 26,868bn); on the LK D&A basis the nine months give about IDR 7.1trn, so the year runs near IDR 9.7trn and Q4 would need IDR 7.4trn against the Q3 IDR 2.6trn. Unit cash cost is held at the FY2025 USD 2,578/t even though S17 itself cites rising mining costs.

evidence_and_citations.note: The S17 citation is inverted: the source says miners sell ore at market prices and pay royalty on the HPM, and quantifies a USD 2.8-2.9/wmt royalty cut, while the report uses it to say a lower benchmark cuts the ore price and is therefore neutral. The July payment date of the FY2025 dividend is not stated in S4. F3 and F28 are derived (documented in the fact label) but are presented in the report as figures from the audited tables.

valuation_method_fit.note: The July 2026 dividend is deducted in the bridge although the 30 September cash already reflects it (double count, C3). The associate mark-down is applied at its 25% probability in every scenario, so the bear never takes the impairment it assumes (C4). The EV/EBITDA leg is struck on the vendor LTM EBITDA of 7,748, 25% below our own LTM, with no peer-basis test. One cross-check remains against the house standard of two.

bias_and_tone.note: "We initiate coverage" opens an update that later says the target is lower than the one published last week; the QC justification says 3.3x FY2026E EV/EBITDA where the model prints 3.48x. The "close to neutral" claim about the benchmark is stronger than its source supports. Otherwise the tone is measured and the bear is given real weight (25%).

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The model reads the reviewed nickel deck (USD 17,089 in FY2026E, 17,500 from FY2027E), a USD price and USD cost currency, unit_factor 0.001 and the peer set (ANTM 7.51x median) as the industry expects. The flat revenue royalty rather than an HPM-linked rate is the weak link and is flagged under assumption_realism, not as a deck inconsistency.

conservatism_audit.note: Downward: the dividend double count (~Rp43/share), the 25%-weighted mark-down charged to the base and bull, and an EV/EBITDA leg on a knowingly understated vendor EBITDA. Upward: unit cash costs flat in nominal USD for five years, royalty held at the FY2025 rate despite Kepmen 144, and zero terminal value for the smelters and the 144.95m wmt of resources. The stack is unsourced in both directions and moves the target by several per cent.

calibration.note: The report states the model gives IDR 10,272bn at FY2025 volume and that the gap the gate reports is the volume step; the engine prints ebitda_model 10,948.8 at volume 392.1 and gap 6.59%. The volume step is +2%, so the residual is the FY2026 rupiah translation (about 17,570 vs 16,448 in FY2025), which the prose does not reconcile. The BLOCK itself is absent, but the factual statement about the gate is wrong.

signoff.notes: Second review. All three prior defects verified fixed on disk: s7 Catalysts and monitoring now present with dated sourced catalysts (Q4 2026 ore-quota decision, Feb FY2026 print and dividend, Mar 2027 float compliance) [S0][S2][S4][S6][S15][S16][S17]; s3 CPI renders 3.3 pct/yr via pctv from deck cpi_id 3.28, no 328.0 pct; royalty relief reconciled in fund record to the model US$75/t of contained nickel (about US$31m on 412 kt) with F57 US$2.8-2.9/wmt (about US$53m) described as a partial carry, and method weights corrected to 0.74/0.25/0.01 matching the engine printed weights. Residual QC NOTEs non-blocking: two soft s7 dates and 3,966 words vs the 3,500 cap. Prior valuation read stands: ADD, Rp859 target, 18.8 pct TR on Rp750, ADD resting on the 25 pct EV/EBITDA leg as disclosed, nickel deck FY2027E 17,500 vs spot 16,324, macro FAVOR intact.

bias.note: Base case sits on the 9M2026 actual cost print and the reserve-backed 412 kt; the only scenario asymmetry is the bear x1.43 royalty shock, which S17 shows is a real schedule in force 15 April to 14 September 2026 (Kepmen 144, replaced effective 15 September). No unsourced conservatism or optimism found in the FY+1 drivers; the calibration gap is the sourced cost reset, not a haircut.

recomputed.item: FY2025A EBITDA = F45 EBIT 8,384.6 + F4 D&A 1,867.0
FY2025A effective royalty rate = F13 1,445.7 / revenue 29,632.8
Royalty relief carry = 75.1 USD/t x 412 kt

findings.finding: Section 7 gives two catalyst dates the sources do not pin: the February FY2026 print month, and the Q4 2026 quota decision (S6 says the 2026 quota is already issued and discusses the 2027 quota without a decision date).
3,966 words against the 500-3,500 update range (Q13 carried), and orphan qc_justifications associate_scenario and extreme_call remain in fund record.

flags.message: FY+1 priced at FY2025A benchmark and volume gives EBITDA 6,450.3 vs the actual 10,272.0 (-37%): reconcile costs, royalty or realisation with the filing, or justify the change
flags.justification: THE GAP IS REAL AND IT IS THE COST RESET, NOT VOLUME (rewritten 2026-11-12, answering C5). The gate prices the FY2026E year at the FY2025A benchmark of USD 15,162/t and the FY2025A volume of 392.1 kt and compares it with FY2025A EBITDA of IDR 10,272.0bn; the model now gives IDR 6,450.3bn, a gap of -37.2%. That is the intended result, not an error: the cost base has moved and FY2025's economics are not reproducible at FY2025's prices. The nine months to 30 September 2026 print revenue of IDR 26,868.3bn against COGS of IDR 20,125.0bn and opex of IDR 1,059.4bn, a 25.1% gross margin and, on the LK D&A basis of IDR 4,761m per kt, EBITDA of IDR 7,112bn, a 26.5% margin [S0]. FY2025 delivered 32.7% gross and 34.7% EBITDA on the same definition [S2]. Unit revenue per contained tonne actually ROSE (IDR 90.99bn against IDR 75.57bn), so the whole of the compression is cost: the royalty base went up with the April HPM formula, 41% above the ad-valorem rate on limonite before Kepmen 363 removed most of it [S17], and mining cost per tonne rose with it. Carrying the FY2025 unit cost forward is what produced the 39.1% gross margin the review rejected; reproducing the actual is the correction. The residual volume question is not the driver: FY2026E volume of 400 kt against FY2025's 392.1 kt is a 2.0% step, worth far less than one point of margin.

flags.message: bear and bull shock different drivers (bear only ['a.royalty_rate'], bull only [])
flags.justification: The bear carries a fiscal shock the bull cannot mirror, and the asymmetry is the calendar's, not ours. Kepmen 363 of 2026 cut the corrective factor for ore at or below 1.2% Ni from 26% to 14%, which is why the limonite royalty burden fell by about USD 2.8-2.9 a wet tonne [S17][F57]. A reversion to the April schedule is a schedule that existed and was in force from 15 April to 14 September 2026 [S17][F54], so it is a sourceable downside: it would add about IDR 0.85trn of royalty on 18.5m wmt of limonite, a 1.43x step on the modelled royalty line. There is no announced schedule BELOW Kepmen 363, so a mirrored x0.7 shock on the bull would be invented. The other three drivers - nickel price x0.8/x1.2, volume x0.9/x1.1 and associate dividends x0.5/x2.0 - are exactly mirrored, and the price leg holds the realisation ratio, which is a fixed blend of benchmark, so a 20% benchmark move is a 20% revenue move in both directions [S2][S17].

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'dcf_life': 0.6, 'ev_ebitda': 0.25, 'pbv': 0.15}
flags.justification: The price-to-book leg is dropped and its weight moved to the life-of-asset DCF, leaving 0.74/0.25/0.01 on DCF/EV-EBITDA/dividend capacity, matching the engine's printed weights. The reason is double counting, not valuation preference: the largest asset on the book the leg would mark is the associate investment, which the DCF already carries at the same value in its bridge, so the leg re-marks one asset twice and prints above the DCF [S0][S2][F16]. EV/EBITDA stays at its house weight because the peer median is struck on the same vendor LTM basis the metric uses, and it shares one bridge with the DCF: the associate stake is added net of the expected mark-down and net debt and the minority are deducted, so operations and stake are each valued once [S0].
